research_question: 能否用计算便宜的初始构型局部指标预测 repeatable IK 整个 Q-loop 长度，以快速筛选较短周期关节轨迹起点？

title: Global Redundancy Resolution via Continuous Pseudoinversion of the Forward Kinematic Map
authors: Hauser, Kris; Emmons, Scott
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
version_or_date: Author preprint corresponding to IEEE TASE 2018; title/author/abstract/12-page contents checked; not line-by-line compared with VoR
research_question: Can a workspace-wide continuous right inverse of forward kinematics be constructed for redundant manipulators so repeated workspace points map to consistent configurations, while accounting for free-space constraints?
robot_and_task_assumptions: Fixed-base redundant serial manipulators; position-only 2D/3D tasks and one 6D pose Baxter extension; joint bounds and collision-free configurations define free space. Global map is attempted over a sampled reachable workspace.
ik_representation: Discrete workspace graph and C-space roadmap; sample multiple IK configurations per workspace node, test local path visibility by midpoint IK and recursive bisection, then assign a configuration sheet minimizing unresolved edges before interpolation/projection.
branch_and_singularity_handling: Directly targets workspace-wide single-valued continuous pseudoinverse when topologically feasible. Unresolved/disconnected edges mark discontinuity regions, which can occur near singularities, joint bounds, or collision boundaries. It minimizes breaks if a global section is impossible; no singularity crossing state machine or proof.
joint_constraints: Joint limits and self/environment collision are encoded as free-space feasibility. No speed, acceleration, torque, or dynamics constraints.
method_and_guarantees: CSP/MAX-CSP assignment with heuristic descent, min-conflicts, and coordinate descent for path length. Roadmap sampling and heuristic search are not complete or globally optimal; the continuous extension between samples is not certified over the whole domain.
evaluation_and_results: Planar 3R path length reduced about 60% and disconnected edges about 24%; planar 20R unresolved edge fraction reduced from 3.69% to 0.96% and path length about 38%. Across 3D models unresolved-edge fractions ranged Jaco 0.062% to Robosimian 13.9%. Baxter 6D extension used 451,440 workspace nodes and 200 IK samples/node, taking about four days in the reported setup.
evidence_type: Algorithm and simulations/model-based workspace analyses; workspace design examples with robot models, not physical closed-loop trajectory execution validation.
authors_stated_limitations: Roadmap must contain necessary configurations and visibility paths; narrow passages need denser sampling. CSP search is heuristic and NP-hard, so neither completeness nor a global optimum is guaranteed. Large 6D problems incur substantial runtime and memory cost.
review_relevance: Core reference for pointwise vs pathwise vs global IK and repeated workspace-point consistency; demonstrates topology/free-space limits on continuous solution maps. Not a time-parameterized trajectory optimizer or certified singularity-crossing method.

title: On Higher Order Inverse Kinematics Methods in Time-Optimal Trajectory Planning for Kinematically Redundant Manipulators
authors: Reiter, Alexander; Mueller, Andreas; Gattringer, H.
version_or_date: Author-uploaded preprint corresponding to IEEE TII 2018; identity checked against DOI/title/authors/abstract; not line-by-line compared with VoR
research_question: How to formulate time-optimal path following for redundant manipulators while enforcing sufficient trajectory smoothness and robot technological limits, and derive consistent higher-order IK relations for optimization?
robot_and_task_assumptions: Fixed-base 4R planar SCARA position-only quarter-circle rest-to-rest case; plus spatial Stäubli TX90L on linear axis (1P+6R), elliptical 5D task, rest-to-rest. Rigid links/ideal joints for inverse dynamics; C4 trajectory case; 200 uniform shooting intervals.
ik_representation: Joint Space Decomposition (JSD): split redundant/nonredundant coordinates and invert J_nr to derive higher derivatives; Nullspace Method (NM): qdot=J+V+A gamma and analytically differentiate the same velocity solution through acceleration, jerk, jounce.
branch_and_singularity_handling: No discrete IK branch labels, periodic closure, or branch transition policy. JSD may have algorithmic singularities when selected J_nr is singular even if full robot is regular; some decompositions fail. No singular-manifold transition guarantee.
joint_constraints: NLP includes joint position and derivative bounds, actuator torque limits through rigid-link inverse dynamics, endpoint conditions; spatial position/velocity settings use 90% of manufacturer limits. Acceleration is also bounded indirectly by torque.
method_and_guarantees: Direct multiple shooting with RK4, CasADi automatic differentiation, IPOPT; minimize terminal time subject to path following, monotonic path parameter, joint/derivative and torque constraints. Nonconvex NLP results are local numerical results, with no global optimality or continuous-time certification.
evaluation_and_results: Planar 4R SCARA C2/C3/C4 times about 0.9635/1.0030/1.0747 s; C4 JSD CPU roughly 59-68 s versus NM 5578 s. Some JSD coordinate splits infeasible, singular, or nonconvergent. Spatial best JSD C4 time 1.0253 s; many splits have singular/convergence issues; exact-derivative NM C4 ran out of memory. C4 JSD trajectory executed on TX90L+linear axis with PD and feedforward torque; authors report negligible lag for most uses, dependent on model fidelity.
evidence_type: Analytical derivation, nonconvex numerical optimization, and one reported physical TX90L-plus-linear-axis C4 trajectory tracking validation; planar SCARA evaluation is model-based.
authors_stated_limitations: JSD depends on coordinate selection and can hit algorithmic singularities or fail convergence; adaptive coordinate selection proposed as future work. NM has high computation and memory burden. NLP minima may be nonglobal; actuator-force higher-order continuity left for future work; accurate inverse dynamics parameters are important for hardware tracking.
review_relevance: Important adjacent/core-context method for derivative-consistent trajectory-level IK with joint/dynamic constraints and C4 physical tracking. It does not solve trajectory-consistent discrete branch tracking, cyclic closure, collision handling, or singularity crossing. One physical example has a translating rail base.

title: Inverse Kinematics with Forward Dynamics Solvers for Sampled Motion Tracking
authors: Scherzinger, Stefanie; Roennau, A.; Dillmann, R.
version_or_date: arXiv author manuscript v2 of the ICAR 2019 paper; PDF header contains conference citation and DOI; not line-by-line compared with IEEE VoR
research_question: How to compute IK for discretely sampled Cartesian targets while making the resulting intermediate joint/task-space motion smooth and goal-directed, without decoupled pointwise IK outputs?
robot_and_task_assumptions: Fixed-base 6R Universal Robots UR10 model; target poses sampled at low or high frequency. Kinematics from ROS UR package/KDL; virtual solver dynamics omit gravity and Coriolis and reset velocity each inner integration step.
ik_representation: Iterative Jacobian-transpose control through virtual forward dynamics: qddot=H^-1 J^T(Kp epsilon + Kd epsdot); virtual mass/inertia concentrated on end effector to homogenize JH^-1J^T. Each next target uses a current q seed and iterative integration.
branch_and_singularity_handling: No explicit branch labels, branch costs, transition logic, or cycle closure. Current configuration initialization and local iteration can promote local continuation but provide no global branch guarantee. Jacobian transpose avoids explicit inverse, but no singularity-transition theorem or singular crossing experiment is provided.
joint_constraints: No hard joint position, velocity, acceleration, torque, or obstacle constraints. Virtual inertia is deliberately not the real mass distribution and omits gravity/Coriolis; it shapes the solver rather than certifying physical dynamics.
method_and_guarantees: Algorithm 1 iteratively forms Cartesian error and its finite difference, virtual force, qddot, and a reset-velocity displacement. Gains, inner step size, and iteration count tune from a one-shot solver to smoothing interpolation. No proof of branch consistency or constrained feasibility.
evaluation_and_results: UR10 kinematic/model evaluation compares with Jacobian transpose. 100,000 random joint configurations show the end-effector-concentrated virtual inertia homogenizes JH^-1J^T. A 150-iteration distant-target test reduces overshoot and preserves rotational-error behavior; square-corner interpolation (1000 intermediate samples per edge) gives more goal-directed paths; 0.2 m/s square target at 100 Hz shows gain-controlled delay/smoothing trade-off. No clearly documented hardware encoder/protocol evidence in the paper.
evidence_type: Analytical derivation and numerical/controller evaluation using UR10 model/kinematics; authors describe experiments and provide a ROS-control implementation, but the reported figures do not clearly establish physical robot execution evidence.
authors_stated_limitations: The mass-matrix inverse adds per-cycle cost; empirically acceptable at reported 10 kHz solver iterations on i7-4900MQ, but a convergence/computation ratio comparison is future work. Gravity/Coriolis are omitted; virtual inertial parameters are unrealistic and empirical gains require tuning.
review_relevance: Adjacent background on local sampled-path smoothing and IK solver conditioning. It does not provide explicit multi-branch tracking, singularity transitions, cyclic closure, or joint/dynamic hard constraints.
evidence_locators: Sec.I pp.1-2; Sec.II-III Eqs.(1)-(16) Figs.1-2 pp.2-4; Sec.IV Algorithm 1 p.4; Sec.V Figs.3-8 pp.4-6; Sec.VI pp.6-7; Sec.VII p.7.

title: Inverse Kinematics of Redundant Manipulators With Dynamic Bounds on Joint Movements
authors: Faroni, M.; Beschi, M.; Pedrocchi, N.

title: A Modified DLS Scheme With Controlled Cyclic Solution for Inverse Kinematics in Redundant Robots
authors: Safeea, Mohammad; Béarée, Richard; Neto, P.
version_or_date: Arts et Métiers Science Arts & Métiers repository author-deposited version; 10-page PDF cover records IEEE TII 17(12), 8014-8023 (2021)
research_question: How can position-level DLS IK prevent joint-space drift when a redundant manipulator repeatedly tracks a closed end-effector path?
robot_and_task_assumptions: Fixed-base serial redundant arms: modified 9-DoF KUKA iiwa simulation and fixed-base 7-DoF KUKA iiwa 14R820 experiment. Repeated circular EEF path with fixed orientation; the solver uses a designated cycle-start configuration q_s.
ik_representation: Iterative position-level DLS with J*=Jᵀ(JJᵀ+λ²I)⁻¹ and null-space feedback q_(k+1)=q_s+(I-κN)(q_k-q_s)-J*(x_k-x_g). Current joint feedback initializes each target solve; N is formed using Jacobian SVD.
branch_and_singularity_handling: Anchors redundant self-motion toward the cycle-start posture and thereby controls cyclic drift/swivel drift. No explicit discrete-branch enumeration/labels or branch-switch logic. Authors state DLS immunity to singularities and demonstrate a path for which fixing the redundant axis makes a 6-DoF version singular; this is regularization/redundancy evidence, not a general singularity-transition or branch-continuity theorem.
joint_constraints: No explicit hard joint-position, velocity, acceleration, torque, or collision constraints; anchoring to q_s does not certify constraint feasibility.
method_and_guarantees: Adds null-space attraction to iterative damped least squares. The paper's linearized kinematic error-state analysis proves stability when 0≤κ≤1. It reports higher compute cost than DLS due mainly to null-space projection, reducible by using SVD for both N and J*. The proof does not establish global constrained IK or a general closure-error bound for arbitrary paths.

title: A comparison of methods solving repeatable inverse kinematics for robot manipulators
authors: Dulęba, I.; Karcz-Dulęba, I.
version_or_date: Publisher version; Archives of Control Sciences 28(LXIV), no. 1, 2018, pp. 5–18; Consensus record listed 2023
research_question: 比较 Jacobian augmentation 与 elastic-band continuation 两种 repeatable IK 方法，考察它们构造闭合 configuration-space Q-loop 的准确度、成功率、路径长度与计算时间。
robot_and_task_assumptions: 固定基座平面 serial revolute pendula；3R 与 5R，2D 末端位置任务；各连杆长1；闭合圆形或矩形 X-loop，并给定 entry configuration q(0)。假设关节运动不受限；无时间参数化、动力学或实机验证。
ik_representation: Repeatable IK 明确定义为 k(q(s))=x(s) 且 q(0)=q(smax)。Method 1 以人工 k_add(q) 扩充运动学并拟合 augmented Jacobian 的右逆；Method 2 用线性插值表示 Q-loop，逐次定位最大 task-space 误差点，以相邻关节构型插值作 Newton IK 初值，并最小化到两邻点的平方距离后插入。
branch_and_singularity_handling: Method 2 从给定 q(0) 延续局部 configuration-space 路径并保持首尾同构型，但无显式离散 IK branch 标签或跨支路策略。Method 1 在 augmented Jacobian 非奇异区给局部唯一逆，但增加 rank(J_aug)<n 的 algorithmic singularities；Method 2 不增加额外奇异集。两法仍会受原 task Jacobian rank(J)<m 的奇异构型影响，均无穿越/转换保证。
joint_constraints: 未建模 joint position/velocity/acceleration/torque/collision 约束；仿真假设 unlimited joint motion。
method_and_guarantees: Method 1 用线性/二次多项式近似附加运动学，将选定区域内 J_add 拟合到 orthonormal augmentation 所需矩阵并反复重优化。Method 2 初始化 L_disc={(0,q0),(smax,q0)}，积分 task-space loop 误差，取最大误差点，以 q1/q2 邻点距离平方和作 null-space 二级目标，插点直到误差低于 rho。作者把误差单调下降作为收敛依据；不能据此声称奇异穿越或关节有界保证。

title: Constrained-Differential-Kinematics-Decomposition-Based NMPC for Online Manipulator Control with Low Computational Costs
authors: Reinhold, Jan; Baumann, H.; Meurer, T.
version_or_date: KITopen publisher-version PDF, 24 pages; published 2023-01-03; CC BY 4.0; repository DOI 10.5445/IR/1000155767.
research_question: Can decomposing an industrial manipulator differential kinematics into translational and rotational subsystems reduce constrained NMPC online computation while retaining joint and Cartesian constraints, obstacle avoidance, and end-effector orientation?
robot_and_task_assumptions: Fixed-base Stäubli TX2-90 six-revolute-joint anthropomorphic arm with spherical wrist (m=3 translation, o=3 orientation); Gazebo/ROS simulation. A preplanned point-to-point tool trajectory is adapted around four spherical fixed or moving obstacles; optional wrist-point height bounds are used.
ik_representation: Geometric decomposition: compute the wrist point from the desired tool pose, solve the first-three-joint anthropomorphic arm and last-three-joint spherical wrist separately. Up to four shoulder/elbow choices times wrist top/bottom give at most eight IK configurations for a pose.
branch_and_singularity_handling: Reject terminal IK solutions outside joint-position bounds. For each remaining terminal solution, construct a 7th-degree joint-space polynomial from the measured initial configuration, match q/qdot/qddot/jerk at both ends (zero endpoint acceleration/jerk), sample it to reject shoulder/elbow/wrist jumps, then choose the trajectory maximizing the worst sampled joint-limit margin. This is discrete branch selection and jump screening for one PTP connection, not general multi-waypoint branch continuation, loop closure, or certified singularity transition. Arm NMPC regularizes inputs and optionally manipulability; quaternion Jacobian-transpose wrist controller avoids Jacobian inversion and authors state it can cross singularities, but no transition metric/test is reported.
joint_constraints: Arm OCP explicitly bounds q_m position and velocity input and includes acceleration/jerk inequalities. Initial branch selector maximizes sampled joint-position margin. Optional wrist-point height and inflated spherical obstacle-distance constraints are included. Wrist q_o limits are only described as delegated to the standard controller in Table 1; no equivalent constrained optimizer formulation or torque-limit guarantee is reported.
method_and_guarantees: Separate reduced translational NMPC for the wrist point (differential Jacobian, quadratic input/acceleration/tracking cost, direct multiple shooting) and unit-quaternion error Jacobian-transpose controller for wrist orientation. A Lyapunov derivative is derived for the orientation controller. Guarantees remain limited to the stated controller properties and simulated setup; no formal branch-continuity, singularity-transition, whole-arm collision, or dynamic-feasibility certificate.
evaluation_and_results: 24-page published-version article. Gazebo/ROS simulation of one Stäubli TX2-90, MATLAB/CasADi/IPOPT on Ubuntu 18.04, Intel Core i7-8550U, 16 GB RAM. Table 3 mean solve times (decomposed vs full NMPC): no obstacle N=100/200 ms: 26±1/130±12 and 30±2/216±21 ms; obstacle: 27±2/153±53 and 33±2/209±9; obstacle+height constraints: 29±2/230±136 and 36±6/284±112. Comparison objectives differ; optimizer runs to convergence, not a WCET bound. Tracking and obstacle examples are plotted; no RMS/max tracking statistic, collision-rate statistic, clearance distribution, hardware test, or repeated-run statistics. Moving obstacles tested at stated velocities; trajectories detour and briefly pause when a corridor closes.
evidence_type: Peer-reviewed open-access journal article; full 24-page publisher-version PDF read. Numerical results and trajectory figures are simulation evidence only; no hardware experiment.
authors_stated_limitations: The work is described as a proof of concept evaluated in simulation. Future work includes a real experiment, transfer from MATLAB and ROS/Gazebo to faster software/hardware, alternative solvers, motion-tracking obstacle updates, and extensions such as self-collision avoidance. Data are available from the corresponding author upon request.
review_relevance: Full-text assessment: Core evidence, narrow scope. Direct evidence for discrete IK terminal-configuration selection, sampled jump screening, joint-limit-margin selection, and constrained point-to-point trajectory generation. It does not establish generalized solution-branch tracking through arbitrary Cartesian paths or singularity transitions.

research_question: How cuspidal 6R kinematics affect IK-solution identification, prescribed Cartesian path feasibility/repeatability, and robot cuspidality decisions.
robot_and_task_assumptions: Fixed-base generic 6R DH serial manipulator; prescribed Cartesian path with no arbitrary deviation; open paths, one-time closed loops, and repetitive closed loops distinguished. Illustrations include Jaco Gen2, FANUC CRX-10ia/L, and UR5-like models.

branch_and_singularity_handling: Defines nonsingular solution change as a joint path avoiding det(J)=0. Cuspidal robots can connect distinct IKS inside one aspect. Open/closed path flowcharts check connectivity from initial through low-IK-count waypoint to final IKS and separately test repeatability.
joint_constraints: Joint limits can affect cuspidality and are included as geometric bounds in the optimal-path-planning formulation. Link-link collision impacts reachable workspace but is nonsmooth/nonalgebraic and is not fully handled in the certified algebraic method. No general velocity/acceleration/torque-constrained online tracking controller.
method_and_guarantees: For generic 6R robots, discretizes workspace and searches a nonsingular path between same-pose IKS by maximizing minimum signed det(J); trajectory state includes q,q',q'' and q''' as input. title: Globally Optimal Solution to Inverse Kinematics of 7DOF Serial Manipulator
authors: Trutman, Pavel; Din, M. El; Henrion, D.; Pajdla, T.
version_or_date: - Pavel Trutman, M. El Din, D. Henrion, and T. Pajdla, IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (2022), DOI [10.1109/LRA.2022.3163444](https://doi.org/10.1109/lra.2022.3163444). - Read matching-title arXiv author preprint [arXiv:2007.12550v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.12550), posted 2020. It matches the DOI title, but the 2022 Version of Record was not compared line by line; claims below are bounded to the preprint.
research_question: Find a globally optimal pointwise IK configuration for a 7R pose under joint-position bounds, minimizing weighted deviation from a preferred configuration. The tested model is a fixed-base KUKA LBR iiwa; poses are sampled independently rather than followed along a prescribed path.
robot_and_task_assumptions: Find a globally optimal pointwise IK configuration for a 7R pose under joint-position bounds, minimizing weighted deviation from a preferred configuration. The tested model is a fixed-base KUKA LBR iiwa; poses are sampled independently rather than followed along a prescribed path.
ik_representation: The authors formulate trigonometric IK as polynomial/semi-algebraic optimization and apply Lasserre moment/SOS relaxations. A degree-reduced formulation reduces relaxation cost.
branch_and_singularity_handling: The objective selects a configuration relative to a reference preference at each pose. It does not assign persistent branch identifiers, continue one branch along a path, or plan branch changes. Multiple pointwise candidates are not branch tracking. No explicit singularity detection, passage, or branch-transition controller is proposed. No pathwise singularity claim is evaluated.
joint_constraints: Joint-angle position limits are explicit inequalities. The formulation does not impose collision/clearance, velocity, acceleration, jerk, torque, or whole-path task constraints. It does not certify a continuous joint lift of a Cartesian path.
method_and_guarantees: The global-optimum claim applies to the pointwise polynomial problem when the chosen relaxation is tight and numerically solved; it is not a path-level guarantee. The degree-reduced order-2 procedure has failures on a small fraction of tested poses.
evaluation_and_results: The preprint tests 10,000 randomly generated KUKA iiwa poses, including feasible and infeasible poses. It reports about 99% solve/infeasibility-certification success for the degree-reduced approach at relaxation order 2; median pose errors and solve times are tabulated. The method is positioned as offline rather than an online path tracker (Sec. IV and results tables).
evidence_type: Full preprint; computational evaluation
authors_stated_limitations: The paper discusses the high computational cost of moment/SOS methods and motivates degree reduction; the evaluated relaxation still has failures and is not positioned as online trajectory planning. No collision or trajectory-level evaluation is reported.
review_relevance: Adjacent evidence for globally optimizing a constrained, redundant single-pose IK objective. It does not establish branch identity, singularity passage, or executable whole-path feasibility.
evidence_locators: - Polynomial formulation and optimization: Secs. II–III. - Degree-reduced relaxation and convergence/failure behavior: Sec. III and Sec. IV tables. - Random-pose evaluation and conclusion: Secs. IV and VIII.

authors: Wenger, P.; Chablat, D.
research_question: 具体问题：解释机器人如何在不经过奇异位形时改变运动学解，以及这种 cuspidality 对机器人设计、规定路径可行性与重复执行的影响。

title: Direct Collocation Methods for Trajectory Optimization in Constrained Robotic Systems
authors: Bordalba, Ricard; Schoels, Tobias; Ros, L.; Porta, J.; Diehl, M.
research_question: 具体问题：直接配点/轨迹优化在含闭环、非完整约束的机器人系统上会产生约束流形漂移；比较并改进 basic、Baumgarte、PKT、projection 和 local-coordinates transcription，使优化轨迹保持在非线性约束流形上。
robot_and_task_assumptions: 机器人：示例包括五杆平行机器人（5 个转动关节、2 个驱动）、四轮 Mecanum 车（车体 3 自由度+4 轮角，4 个轮力矩输入，非完整约束）以及两台 Franka Emika 7-DOF 臂协同搬运气瓶（14 个关节、6 个闭环约束）；其中双臂系统是冗余/高自由度场景，但论文不是通用冗余 IK 求解器。
ik_representation: IK 类型：不是 pose-level IK；是含动力学、控制和代数约束的 direct trajectory optimization/collocation。初始猜测可由满足约束的 kinodynamic planner 或粗网格 projection warm start 提供。
branch_and_singularity_handling: 分支：未提出 IK branch tracking/switching；局部坐标图和最近投影有助于保持局部连续，但不同流形分支/同伦类由初始猜测决定，不做全局分支搜索。
joint_constraints: 约束：处理 holonomic/nonholonomic 约束、动力学、闭环、轮胎无滑移、边界/路径约束及电机力矩界；双臂示例受驱动力矩和末端静止边界约束，代价用控制平方或控制导数平方促进平滑。速度/加速度来自动力学变量，未建立普适的工业 joint-limit/jerk 安全证书。
method_and_guarantees: 连续性/执行保证：local-coordinates 方法按构造使 spline 全程落在 X，projection 只保证 knot states、区间内仍有漂移；作者定义并积分运动学误差 EK 与动力学误差 ED。该保证是光滑流形与数值模型下的几何/离散化性质，不是碰撞、硬件、全局最优或 IK branch 可执行性证明。

title: J-PARSE: Jacobian-based Projection Algorithm for Resolving Singularities Effectively in Inverse Kinematic Control of Serial Manipulators
authors: Guptasarma, Shivani; Strong, M.; Zhen, Honghao; Kennedy, Monroe
version_or_date: - Shivani Guptasarma, M. Strong, Honghao Zhen, and Monroe Kennedy, [arXiv:2505.00306v6](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00306), revised 22 September 2026; DOI [10.48550/arXiv.2505.00306](https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2505.00306). Preprint. - Read the complete v6 arXiv PDF.
research_question: Stabilize first-order Cartesian velocity IK for fixed-base serial manipulators near workspace/internal singularities, including target poses on or outside workspace boundaries. The paper studies 2R models and physical X-Arm7 and Kinova Gen3 robots.
robot_and_task_assumptions: Stabilize first-order Cartesian velocity IK for fixed-base serial manipulators near workspace/internal singularities, including target poses on or outside workspace boundaries. The paper studies 2R models and physical X-Arm7 and Kinova Gen3 robots.
ik_representation: An SVD “Safety Jacobian” floors small singular values at a fraction γ of the maximum, separates singular and nonsingular task directions, scales commands in singular directions, and applies a right inverse in the remaining directions. A projected null-space potential can bias posture toward a nominal configuration.
branch_and_singularity_handling: This is local velocity control, not a global branch planner. A nominal posture potential can favor an elbow-up configuration in examples, but context-aware branch-exit selection and redundancy-wide stability are left open. The method enables stable approach to and departure from near-boundary/internal singular configurations under stated assumptions. Exact singular starts are treated separately; motion in a lost task direction can remain unavailable. This is local singularity-robust control, not global branch transition.
joint_constraints: The stability/velocity analysis is explicitly scoped without joint limits and collision constraints. Joint-position feasibility, self/external collision, full path planning, and global branch selection are not enforced. The projected potential is not a hard-constraint certificate.
method_and_guarantees: The paper gives local stability and local asymptotic-stability results for stated nonsingular-start assumptions, including near-singular operation, with a sufficient discrete-time step bound and a velocity bound depending on γ. These are local controller guarantees, not whole-path realization under joint/collision constraints.
evaluation_and_results: Simulations and physical X-Arm7/Kinova Gen3 demonstrations include teleoperation/visual-servo motions near boundary or internal singular configurations. A diffusion-policy task reports fetching success in 9/10 trials (Secs. VIII–X). Tests show local behavior, not hard-constrained path planning.
evidence_type: Full preprint; theory, simulation, hardware
authors_stated_limitations: The paper leaves feasible-path identification under collision and joint limits, context-aware branch selection, and broader redundancy analysis to future work. It also notes acceleration discontinuity at the threshold while arguing it does not invalidate the stated stability result.
review_relevance: Strong adjacent evidence for singularity-robust local control, including hardware. It shows singularity handling exists, but does not resolve branch identity or joint/collision-constrained path feasibility.
evidence_locators: - Safety Jacobian and stability conditions: Secs. III–V. - Exact/near singular behavior and assumptions: Secs. VI–VII. - X-Arm7/Kinova evaluations: Secs. VIII–X. - Scope limits/conclusion: Secs. X–XI.

title: Path Planning and Optimization for Cuspidal 6R Manipulators
authors: Elias, Alexander; Wen, John
version_or_date: - Alexander J. Elias and John T. Wen, [arXiv:2501.18505v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.18505), 29 April 2025; DOI [10.48550/arXiv.2501.18505](https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2501.18505). Preprint. - Read the complete v2 arXiv PDF. Demonstrations use software/simulation environments; no physical robot trial is reported.
research_question: Determine whether a prescribed workspace path admits a continuous joint-space realization on cuspidal 6R arms, where pose-wise IK feasibility does not imply a continuous lift. Examples include ABB GoFa, FANUC CRX, ABB IRB6640, and three-parallel-axis families.
robot_and_task_assumptions: Determine whether a prescribed workspace path admits a continuous joint-space realization on cuspidal 6R arms, where pose-wise IK feasibility does not imply a continuous lift. Examples include ABB GoFa, FANUC CRX, ABB IRB6640, and three-parallel-axis families.
ik_representation: Compute IK solutions at samples along the Cartesian path, build a directed acyclic graph whose nodes are sampled solutions, connect adjacent candidates when wrapped joint change meets a threshold, and solve a shortest-path problem for a chosen cost such as finite-difference joint velocity. An outer derivative-free optimizer shifts the toolpath in the robot base frame and reruns the graph planner.
branch_and_singularity_handling: Explicitly enumerates multiple IK solutions per sample and links them into a discrete solution graph. This is direct path-level branch selection. Branch identity is induced by thresholded edges, not a persistent analytic label. The planner can seek nonsingular paths by rejecting determinant-sign changes, or permit graph paths through singularities by removing that restriction. Approximate/least-squares IK supports workspace boundary/internal singular cases. The discrete graph does not prove continuous singularity passage between every linked sample.
joint_constraints: Sampled hard/soft joint-position and derivative constraints (including velocity/acceleration-related edge limits) are available in path selection. Collision checks for the end effector and every link are not included in the reported optimizer; the authors list this as future work. No full time-parameterized dynamic or clearance certificate is established.
method_and_guarantees: Shortest-path optimality is over the finite graph and sampled cost. Outer optimization is local derivative-free search, with multiple-minimum sensitivity. Neither stage certifies continuous-time, collision-free constrained execution of the exact Cartesian curve.
evaluation_and_results: Numerical/software demonstrations include GoFa reconfiguration, CRX MoveL feasibility dependent on endpoint branches, an in-workspace infeasible IRB6640 path, and toolpath-placement tests with about 500 samples. Joint-motion objectives improve in examples; multiple local minima motivate multiple starts. No hardware experiment is reported (Secs. III–V and figures).
evidence_type: Full preprint; numerical/software evaluation
authors_stated_limitations: Future work includes collision checks for every link/end effector, time-optimal objectives, and improved sampling/analytic gradients. Toolpath optimization is local and paths are sampled.
review_relevance: Potentially Core-level evidence on branch selection along prescribed paths and singularity-permitting transitions, with sampled joint/derivative constraints. It is the strongest counterexample in this batch to a categorical claim that no method combines these axes. Graph discretization, threshold edges, optional singularity logic, absent collision constraints, and no continuous-time proof keep the finding bounded; the frozen screening label remains Adjacent.
evidence_locators: - Cuspidality/path feasibility: Sec. I. - IK-solution graph and edge/constraint construction: Sec. III. - Robot examples and singularity options: Sec. IV. - Toolpath-placement objective/results/limitations: Sec. V and conclusion.
